- Category: regression
- Severity: medium
- File: `plugins/shipwright-design/skills/design/kit/untitled-ui/kit.css:931`
- Finding: `.list-item[aria-current]` also matches `aria-current="false"`. Consumers that explicitly mark inactive links as false will now display those links as selected.
- Suggestion: Use `.list-item[aria-current]:not([aria-current="false"])` alongside `.list-item.active`, and cover both true and false values.

- Category: test
- Severity: low

- Finding: The regex contains a literal backspace character after `.count`, rather than the intended `\b` word boundary. A global `.count { ... }` rule would therefore pass this scoping test.
- Suggestion: Replace the backspace with `\b` in the raw regex string and verify that a global `.count` rule fails the check.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The diff substantially implements the requested components, but the selection-state regression and ineffective scoping assertion should be corrected before shipping; browser rendering remains unverified.

glm.feedback:
### Findings

- Category: edge-case | Severity: low
  File: `plugins/shipwright-design/skills/design/kit/untitled-ui/kit.css` (`.master-pane { ... margin: calc(-1 * var(--space-2)); }`)
  Finding: The negative margin trick to un-clip shadows/focus rings expands the pane visually outside its grid track on both sides — 8px left of the track and 8px into the 20px gap toward `detail-pane`. In a container without padding, this can cause an 8px horizontal bleed/overflow at the viewport left edge.
  Suggestion: Consider `overflow-y: auto; overflow-x: clip;` with a slightly larger padding-compensation, or add the padding to `.master-detail` itself so the pane's grid track includes the breathing room.

- Category: spec | Severity: low
  File: `plugins/shipwright-design/skills/design/kit/untitled-ui/kit.css` (`.master-detail { grid-template-columns: minmax(280px, 360px) ... }`)
  Finding: AC2 says a "fixed-width list pane"; `minmax(280px, 360px)` makes it fluid within a range, so at container widths between the bounds the pane width changes. This is a partial/loose reading of the AC.
  Suggestion: Either use a fixed track (e.g. `360px`) or note in the docs that "fixed-width" is implemented as a bounded range, so consumers know what to expect.

- Category: test | Severity: low
  File: `plugins/shipwright-design/tests/test_untitled_ui_kit.py:337` (`assert not re.search(r"^\.count", css, re.M)`)
  Finding: This test is the first visible use of `re` in the shown file section; if `import re` isn't already at the top of the file, all four new tests fail with `NameError` at collection time. Also, the pattern only rules out a bare `.count` selector at line start — a rule like `.count, .tab` or `.callout .count` would pass, so the "scoped to the two switchers" claim is only weakly enforced.
  Suggestion: Verify the `re` import exists; strengthen the check to assert no selector list anywhere contains `.count` unscoped (e.g. search for `.count` occurrences and assert each is preceded by `.tab ` or `.segmented-item `).

- Category: test | Severity: low
  File: `plugins/shipwright-design/tests/test_untitled_ui_kit.py:303–310`
  Finding: The narrow-screen test locates the media block via an exact literal `"@media (max-width: 900px) {\n  .master-detail"` — any whitespace/formatting reflow of kit.css breaks the test even when the CSS behavior is unchanged. Tests are asserting the file's byte layout, not the layout behavior.
  Suggestion: Match the `@media` line with a regex tolerant of whitespace, or slice on the `@media (max-width: 900px)` token and its matching closing brace.

- Category: bug | Severity: low
  File: `plugins/shipwright-design/skills/design/kit/untitled-ui/fragments/gallery.html` (copy button `class="btn btn-secondary btn-sm copy-btn copied"` with text "Copied")
  Finding: The gallery shows the button only in its terminal `copied` state; there is no example of the resting `copy-btn` state next to the "Copied" one, so consumers can't see both states side by side, and a class-inventory test reading the gallery cannot verify the un-copied variant appears anywhere.
  Suggestion: Add a second callout (or a second button) in the resting state labelled "Copy" so both states are demonstrated.

No security issues: the diff adds static CSS and HTML with no scripts, no inline handlers, no external assets, and no user-controlled data. No regression risk to existing classes: the only modified existing rule is `.list-item.active` (extended, not narrowed), and the new `.count` rules are scoped, so a global `.count` elsewhere in the kit (if any) is unaffected — though the docs table should arguably state that any pre-existing unscoped `.count` usage would silently not get the badge styling.

Overall: the implementation matches the six ACs, prior review/doubt findings are visibly addressed in the CSS, docs, and gallery, and the tests are narrowly real (they'd catch removal of the collapse rule, the sticky offsets, the contrast pair, and the mono eyebrow). Findings above are refinements, not blockers.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
